messages:
sara: FYI, saw a sharp tail-latency spike in eu-west at ~03:10. Correlated with two large cold-start jobs from tenant atlas-ai. Other tenants in the same slice saw request latencies jump 3-5x for ~90s.

mike: grabbing logs now. which pool?

sara: dedicated-ish shared-slab eu-west-3a, fractional slices. The cold runs were big (long prompt, model-2.1-large) and triggered NVLink mem motion + kvcache churn.

ops-bot: ALERT: pool-eu-west-3a latency anomaly detected (p95 > 600ms) — triggered at 2026-03-18T03:10:12Z

mike: looks like allocator did immediate backfill and evicted low-warmth slots to make room. Evictions + rebinds = extra PCIe churn.

kai: this is the classic cold-start ejection cascade. We have no soft-quarantine on new allocations that cause a spike. Proposal: detect high first-60s resource delta and auto-evict the offending allocation to a cooldown queue or dedicated transient slice.

jess: how does that interact with SLA for premium tenants? we'd need opt-out or pin-to-dedicated for guaranteed low-latency.

kai: agree — default policy: soft-quarantine for non-premium tenants. Premium tenants get either pre-warm or forced dedicated. Also add a probed pre-warm step: small warmup job to load weights into GPUs/kv cache before routing live traffic.

mike: can we implement heuristics quickly? e.g., if allocation causes >20% rise in pool p95 or >X MB kvcache churn in first 60s, then move it to warmup-queue.

sara: yes, metric names: pool.p95.delta_60s, pool.kvcache_churn_bytes. We should also raise an alert on repeated offenders (tenant cold_start_eviction_count > 3 in 1h).

ops-bot: NOTE: added metric cold_start_eviction_count for tenant-level graphing (experimental).

kai: sketch of allocator config I was thinking: 
```
cold_start_policy:
  enabled: true
  detection_window_s: 60
  p95_delta_threshold_pct: 20
  kvcache_churn_threshold_bytes: 500000000 # 500MB
  action: soft_quarantine # choices: soft_quarantine, forced_dedicated, throttle
  quarantine_ttl_s: 120
```

jess: sanity check: soft_quarantine means requests are queued behind a small pre-warm runner and get failed-over to fallback model if warmup not complete within TTL?

kai: yep. Also add fast-fallback to cheaper quantized variant to avoid complete outage.

mike: side note: we should instrument per-allocation warmup latency and track cost delta so finance can see impact (cost-per-coldstart).

sara: action items: 1) short-term: enable metric + alert + temp soft_quarantine on eu-west-3a for non-prem tenants (owner: mike) 2) mid-term: allocator rule + pre-warm probe (owner: kai) 3) product: create opt-out/dedicated SKU + docs (owner: jess)

mike: filing a small incident follow-up doc and will toggle the temp quarantine flag now.

deploy-bot: /deploy feature/eviction-toggle -> success (flags: eu-west-3a.soft_quarantine = true) :rocket:

sara: after enabling, p95 is back to normalish in the last 6m. we'll keep monitoring. thanks team. :thumbsup:

jess: can we add a blurb to onboarding docs about warmup expectations and recommended SKUs for heavy cold-start workloads? I can write that.

kai: Also adding a lightweight simulator to the infra repo to run cold-start probes against staging pools to tune thresholds.

sara: great. tagging this for the next oncall retro.

mike: closing loop — I updated the incident thread with graphs and the temp mitigations. will follow up with a rollout plan for the allocator rule next week.

sara: ok, if no objections I'll leave eu-west-3a soft_quarantine on for 24h and collect data.

jess: fine by me. thanks everyone.
